2027 Season Tickets

Every benefit of holding a Riverhounds season ticket, laid out below, plus what the coming stadium expansion means for your seat.

Become a Season Ticket Holder

Learn About Auto-Renewal

Experience all 17 Riverhounds home games from March through October with season tickets! Starting at just $20 per ticket, per game, season tickets is the best value the club offers. Enjoy your own seat for every match, exclusive Season Ticket Holder benefits and events, first access to playoff tickets and gain priority to future seating opportunities as F.N.B. Stadium expands to 15,000 seats. There’s never been a better time to be a Season Ticket Holder with the Pittsburgh Riverhounds!

Season Ticket Holder Benefits

Priority for the New Stadium Expansion

F.N.B. Stadium is heading toward roughly 15,000 seats. Season Ticket Holders will have top priority when new seating opportunities become available.

Same Seat, Every Game

One reserved seat for the full home schedule.

First Access to Playoff Tickets

First chance to buy before the general public.

Lowest Ticket Pricing Per Match

The best per-game rate the club offers.

Ticket Exchange Program

Swap your seat for a different home date.

Flexible Payment Plans

Spread your season across installments.

Dedicated Account Representative

One contact for your account and seats.

Special Discounts

Savings on merchandise and concessions.

Exclusive Gifts and Team Events

Season ticket only giveaways and meet-ups.

More Perks Added All Year

New benefits get announced as the season goes on.

Explore Your Seating Options

Riverside

Get closer to the action than almost anyone in the stadium. With just two rows running the length of the sideline, Riverside Seating offers an exclusive experience where every seat is within 12 feet of the sideline, putting you right at field level and on top of the action.

Grandstand

There’s no bad seat in the house at F.N.B. Stadium. Grandstand Seating puts you close to the action while offering an unparalleled view of Pittsburgh’s downtown skyline and an unmatched game-day atmosphere. It’s the perfect place to take in every moment of Hounds soccer.

Supporter

Get close to the action and help make F.N.B. Stadium one of the toughest places to play in the USL. Surrounded by the club’s biggest and most passionate fans, this is where you’ll find nonstop singing, chanting and cheering, with drums, flags and smoke filling the section after the match’s biggest moments. If you want to make noise, bring the energy and be part of the action for all 90 minutes, this is your section.

Find Your Seat

Every seating area at F.N.B. Stadium, from the supporters’ end to midfield. Your account representative can walk you through what’s open in each section and what it costs.

Tap the map to open it full size.

.

F.N.B. Stadium Expansion

Pittsburgh Riverhounds SC has unveiled plans for a major South Shore stadium expansion, boosting capacity to 15,000 as the club aims to move into the United Soccer League’s new Division One. The project includes enhanced premium seating, a club with banquet space and luxury suites, all offering fans more ways than ever to experience the action.

The only way to guarantee priority access to these new seats is to be a Riverhounds Season Ticket Holder. The earlier you secure your membership, the higher your priority when new seating locations become available.

Act now and make sure you’re first in line for the future of Riverhounds soccer!

Renewing is easy. Set it up once and we’ll handle the rest, and your dedicated account representative can walk you through the process and answer any questions.

text:
Directions and Parking

FROM EAST OF PITTSBURGH

Take I-376W/U-22W toward Pittsburgh. Take the Grant Street exit (71A) on the left.  Turn left onto Fort Pitt Blvd. Take the first left onto Smithfield Street as it becomes the Smithfield Bridge. Turn right onto E. Carson St. Take the second right into Station Square and turn left onto W. Station Square Dr.

FROM WEST OF PITTSBURGH

Take I-376E toward Pittsburgh. Merge onto US-19 N/PA-51 N/Saw Mill Run Blvd. via exit 69C toward West End. Take the PA-51 N/McKees Rocks/West End ramp. Turn slight right onto US-19 N/PA-51 N/PA-60 S/S Main St. Turn right onto W. Carson St. Turn left onto W. Station Square Dr.

FROM WASHINGTON, PA AND SOUTH

Merge onto I-79N via exit 18 toward Pittsburgh. Merge onto I-376 E/US-30 E/US-22 E via exit 59A toward Pittsburgh.  Merge onto US-19 N/PA-51 N/Saw Mill Run Blvd via exit 69C toward West End. Take the PA-51 N/McKees Rocks/West End ramp. Turn slight right onto US-19 N/PA-51 N/PA-60 S/S Main St. Turn right onto W. Carson St. Turn left onto W. Station Square Dr.

FROM WHEELING, WV AND BRIDGEPORT, OH

Merge onto I-70E crossing into Pennsylvania. Merge onto I-79N via exit 18 toward Pittsburgh. Merge onto I-376E/US-30E/US-22 E via exit 59A toward Pittsburgh. Merge onto US-19N/PA-51N/Saw Mill Run Blvd via exit 69C toward West End. Take the PA-51N/McKees Rocks/West End ramp. Turn slight right onto US-19N/PA-51N/PA-60S/S Main St. Turn right onto W. Carson St. Turn left onto W. Station Square Dr.

Parking

Parking is located in the west lot of Station Square, lying adjacent to the F.N.B. Stadium office building and underneath the Fort Pitt Bridge. Only cash payment is accepted at the parking gate on event days.

Additional parking is available at the following locations in Station Square for standard hourly rates:

Parking garage (across from Sheraton Hotel)

East lot (adjacent to the Smithfield Street Bridge)

West Carson/river lot (adjacent to the Gateway Clipper Fleet Dock Ramp)

Please contact F.N.B. Stadium at (412) 224-4900 for information on event bus/van parking.

text:
Ahl, Mikoy land Team of the Week places

News

Press Releases

Team Announcements
Riverhounds Staff
October 13, 2026 2:30 pm
Share

Owen Mikoy leaps to head the ball in the rain during the Hounds’ 2-1 win over Hartford Athletic last Saturday at F.N.B. Stadium. Mikoy and teammate Charles Ahl were named to the Team of the Week for their performances in the match. (Photo: Chris Cowger/Riverhounds SC)

PITTSBURGH (Oct. 13, 2026)
— Pittsburgh Riverhounds SC midfielder
Charles Ahl
and defender
Owen Mikoy
were selected to the USL Championship Team of the Week for Week 32, the league announced this afternoon.

Ahl was the offensive star Saturday in the Hounds’ 2-1 win over Hartford Athletic that clinched a playoff berth for the team. The second-year pro set up
Trevor Amann
for the opening goal of the match before scoring the game-winning goal in the 66th minute by turning a pass from
Robbie Mertz
into the top of the net from 6 yards out. In addition to his scoring contributions, Ahl was credited with two chances created, four recoveries, won 5 of 9 duels and drew three free kicks for the Hounds.

Mikoy had a nearly flawless night as a ball winner from his center back spot in the victory, recording a season-high 16 clearances and winning 10 of 11 aerial duels for the ball, part of a larger 13-for-14 night on duels. Now an regular starter for the Hounds in his first year as a pro, Mikoy led the team by gaining possession six times, including winning all three of his tackles in the match.

For both players, it is the first time earning a spot in the league’s weekly best 11, though both Ahl and Mikoy did earn bench honors on the Team of the Week once earlier this season.

The Hounds are back in action for their final road match of the regular season when they visit Rhode Island FC on Saturday, Oct. 17 in a 7:30 p.m. matchup with major playoff seeding implications in the Eastern Conference.

attributes.description: After one full year as head coach, Rob Vincent talks about what he's learned and what has changed since assuming the Hounds' lead role.

text:
Vincent reflects on full year in the big chair

Features

News
Riverhounds Staff
October 16, 2026 11:00 am
Share

Hounds head coach Rob Vincent takes notes while watching his team’s 2-1 win over Hartford Athletic last Saturday at F.N.B. Stadium. (Photo: Chris Cowger/Riverhounds SC)

On Oct. 10, 2025, the eve of a crucial match against Indy Eleven,
Rob Vincent
was called into an afternoon meeting at what was still known as Highmark Stadium, where he would receive some news he never expected.

Vincent learned then what the public would find out a few hours later: He had been appointed acting head coach of the Riverhounds while head coach
Bob Lilley
was placed on administrative leave.

The seven weeks that followed became legendary in the club’s history. A win in that first match against Indy helped propel the Hounds to the No. 4 seed in the East, and, as luck would have it, a path through the Eastern Conference Final entirely in Pittsburgh on the way to winning a first-ever league title in dramatic fashion at FC Tulsa in the USL Championship Final.

But after the whirlwind of those first months died down, reality took hold. In December, Vincent was named the club’s head coach on a permanent basis. And at that point, he was now the person in charge of assembling and preparing a team that could defend its USL Championship title.

Fast-forward to today: Vincent has now been in the head coaching role for a full 12 months. He celebrated the occasion with a
2-1 win over Hartford Athletic
that confirmed the Hounds’ return to the playoffs, one year to the day after he assumed the acting head coach role.

So what has changed for Vincent, the youngest Championship-winning coach who turns 36 later this month, after 365 days as the man in charge?

“I think I’ve definitely grown a lot, and it has forced me to be really concrete in my ideas, and some of those ideas have evolved as the season’s gone on,” Vincent said. “I think any first-time head coach is going to have their ideal way of playing, but in practice, you have to adjust. When you’re in the head coach’s role, the learning curve becomes a lot steeper. But with a year under my belt, I feel a lot more prepared to be able to reflect on this season when it ends, and then bring us back even stronger next year.”

The one-year returns on Vincent’s time in charge have been strong. The win over Hartford improved the coach’s record to 19 wins, 12 losses and 11 draws across 42 matches in all competitions. That record works out to 1.67 points per game in the table, the third-best mark in club history behind only Lilley’s 1.71 and the 1.93 total of
Ricardo Iribarren
, whose two full seasons leading the team included the 2004 squad that went 19-3-1 after a drop to the third division.

But one thing Vincent has learned is that being the gaffer is more than setting the practice schedule and making the final decisions on the lineup sheet. The sheer volume of demands on a professional head coach makes time management and organization skills that are just as important as any tactical concerns.

“It was more than I probably expected. You certainly have to learn to delegate some of those responsibilities a little bit more,” Vincent said.

He explained: “A lot of the things I was doing in my assistant coach role, you develop a certain way of doing things, and now you have to hand off those responsibilities to other people. Then you have to start making the big decisions and handle things like media calls, managing the whole staff — the playing staff and the technical staff. It’s all part of the learning curve, and I haven’t gotten it spot-on every time, but I’m trying to grow and learn with each week that goes by, and I certainly feel more prepared now than I was eight months ago.”

By having that added responsibility, it also changes the interpersonal dynamics between Vincent and the players.

As an assistant, Vincent’s age and being the coach on staff whose own playing career ended most recently added a degree of relatability between him and the current players. While that didn’t go away with his promotion to the head coaching role, Vincent now has to weigh that against his role as the authority figure at the top.

“The communication with the players, I think I’ve had to figure out the balance as the season has gone on. How much is too much information, how much is not enough information? That’s both as a collective and on an individual basis,” Vincent said. “You’re always refining that communication process, and obviously, having those individual conversations with players — are they in the team, are they out of the team, what’s their role —
Robbie
(
Mertz
), for one, is playing a different role than he played in previous years. So it’s trying to get the balance right on communication with those players.”

Now isn’t the time for too much reflection, of course, with only two matches remaining in the regular season and playoffs right around the corner. Vincent’s focus, naturally, is on Rhode Island FC this Saturday and earning a home playoff match the highest possible seed in the bracket.

But after crossing the one-year mark, he did afford himself a moment to give the put the past 12 months in perspective.

“In many ways, it feels like it’s only just happened, but in some ways, it feels like this season has been a real long time, as well,” he said. “The focus is so much now on the stretch run, that I haven’t given much thought to what happened at the end of last season.”

attributes.description: Hounds goalkeeper Nico Campuzano was named to the USL Championship Team of the Week after his five-save performance that included a penalty kick stop.

text:
Nico lands Team of the Week spot after PK save

News

Press Releases

Team Announcements
Riverhounds Staff
October 20, 2026 2:30 pm
Share

Hounds goalkeeper Nico Campuzano takes a goal kick against Rhode Island FC last Saturday at Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket, R.I. Campuzano made five saves, including a penalty kick stop, in the 1-1 draw. (Photo: Rhode Island FC)

PITTSBURGH (Oct. 20, 2026)
— Pittsburgh Riverhounds goalkeeper
Nico Campuzano
was named to the USL Championship Team of the Week for Week 33 after his shot-stopping helped the Hounds secure a 1-1 draw on the road at Rhode Island FC last Saturday.

Campuzano produced five saves on the night, none bigger than denying a penalty kick by
Leo Afanso
in the 56th minute when the match was still scoreless. The Hounds keeper correctly dove to his left to stop the shot, which kept the team in position to earn a critical point and preserve an outside chance at a top-four finish and home match to open the playoffs next week.

It was the fifth time this season Campuzano has made five or more saves in a match, and the penalty save was his first of the year, which came on the third PK he has faced in his first season with the Hounds. Campuzano has been named to the Team of the Week three times this season, including his Player of the Week performance back in Week 10 at Louisville.

The Hounds will wrap up the regular season this Saturday, Oct. 24, when they face Birmingham Legion FC at 7 p.m. at F.N.B. Stadium. Tickets for the Fan Appreciation Night match are still available via
Ticketmaster
or by calling the box office at 412-865-GOAL.

attributes.description: Meet the expert technical staff of the Pittsburgh Riverhounds. Learn about the coaches and support team driving our USL Championship success!

text:
Technical Staff

Head Coach Rob Vincent

Rob Vincent is entering his first season as the head coach for the Hounds pro team after two years as the First Team’s assistant coach and six seasons leading ECNL teams in the Riverhounds Development Academy.

Late in the 2025 season, Vincent was named the team’s acting head coach, and the Hounds put together a historic run to close the season. The team went unbeaten in seven matches with Vincent in charge, going 3-0-4 overall and advancing throughout the USL Championship Playoffs — three times prevailing on penalty kicks — to win the club’s first league title. With the victory on penalties in the USL Championship Final, Vincent became the youngest head coach to win a title in league history at 35 years old.

A youth player with Everton, Crewe Alexandra and Stockport County in England, Vincent came to the United States to play college soccer at the University of Charleston (W.Va.) from 2009-12. He starred for the Golden Eagles and was three times named a First Team Division II All-American.

Vincent signed with Hounds in 2013, the same year as the opening of F.N.B. Stadium (then called Highmark Stadium), and played three years for the club. In 2015, the midfielder had a breakout season with 21 goals in all competitions — still tied for the second-most in club history — and was named to the USL All-League First Team.

Prior to the 2016 season, MLS team D.C. United reached a transfer agreement with Hounds to bring Vincent to Washington, and by season’s end, he was a regular starter for playoff-bound United. He began 2017 in a similar role, but he suffered a knee injury in the team’s second match that ended his season.

In 2018, Vincent announced his retirement as a player and returned to the Hounds in his academy role.

Sporting Director Dan Visser

Dan Visser enters his 10th full season with the Hounds and his third as Sporting Director, overseeing the soccer aspect of the club at both the professional and academy levels. He holds bachelor’s degrees in math and economics from Messiah College, and he received his Master of Business Administration from Eastern University (Pa.).

He first came to the club as an assistant coach midway through the 2016 season as part of head coach Dave Brandt’s staff. Prior to arriving in Pittsburgh, Visser also served as an assistant coach under Brandt at the United States Naval Academy during its 2015 campaign.

From 2013-14, Visser was head coach at Eastern Nazarene College, and he began his coaching career as an assistant coach and recruiting coordinator at Eastern University while completing his MBA.

Visser played collegiately as a midfielder at Messiah for four seasons before graduating in 2008. During this period, the team won three national championships and accumulated an 89-6-2 record. The two-time team captain also received Regional All-America honors in 2007.

Goalkeeper Coach Jon Busch

Jon Busch is in his fourth season as the goalkeeper coach for the Hounds. He was previously the goalkeeping coach for Scottish Premiership side Hibernian, and before that, with Indy Eleven in the NASL and USL Championship.

Busch entered coaching after an impressive 21-year professional career that included 14 seasons in MLS. Busch first played in the A-League, where he was named the 2001 A-League Goalkeeper of the Year while helping the Hershey Wildcats reach the league final under Bob Lilley.

He was drafted by the Columbus Crew in the 2002 MLS Super Draft and played there until 2006 before joining the Chicago Fire from 2007-09. In 2008, his best year with the Fire, he was named MLS Goalkeeper of the Year after leading the league in save percentage and tying for the league lead in shutouts. Busch continued his career joining the San Jose Earthquakes in 2010, returning to the Fire in 2015 and finishing with Indy Eleven in 2016-17.

Busch also represented the United States in international play as part of the Under-17 team in the 1993 World Championship. He remained in the U.S. player pool and made his only start at the senior level in 2005, recording a shutout against Colombia, 3-0.

Assistant Coach Adam Mitchell

Adam Mitchell is in his first year with the Hounds, joining the club after spending the past seven seasons at Duquesne University.

During his tenure at Duquesne, the Dukes advanced to the Atlantic 10 Championship Final in 2021, hosted A-10 Tournament matches for the first time in 2022, and spent eight weeks in the Division I national rankings to end an 18-year drought without a Top 25 appearance. In that same span, the Dukes produced a total of 13 all-conference selections; the 2023 A-10 Midfielder of the Year, Ask Ekeland; and the first MLS Draft first-round pick in school history in 2024, Jayden Da.

Mitchell began coaching at Lourdes University in Ohio, where he also completed his master’s degree in organizational leadership in 2017. From there, he coached two seasons at Tiffin University, where he helped the Dragons put together a 15-win season in 2018, during which they were finished No. 18 nationally and earned the top seed in the NCAA Division II Midwest Regional.

As a player, Mitchell finished his college career at Notre Dame College (Ohio), where he helped the Falcons twice reach the NCAA Division II Tournament. As a junior in 2014, he led the Mountain East Conference with 14 goals and was a Third-Team All-American as selected by the National Soccer Coaches Association of America.

Assistant Coach/Riverhounds 2 Coach Josh Kremers

Josh Kremers is in his third year with the Riverhounds organization and his first as the head coach of Riverhounds 2, the club’s team in USL League Two.

Kremers previously was the Riverhounds Academy’s Boys Regional League Director and also coached academy boys teams. In addition to leading Riverhounds 2, Kremers also will serve as an assistant with the Riverhounds First Team.

Kremers comes to the role with USL League Two experience, most recently with FC Carolinas, where he served as the club’s Boys Director of Coaching and helped with their teams in League Two and the USL W League. He was also an assistant coach in 2017-18 with the Charlotte Eagles, who won the League Two title in 2017.

Before entering coaching Kremers was a three-year starter at Messiah College, where he won three national championship during his career from 2010-13.

text:
Boswell sets Steelers field goal record
Oct 18, 2026 at 03:42 PM
Teresa Varley
Steelers.com

Kicker Chris Boswell etched his name in the Steelers record books, passing Gary Anderson (1982-94) for the most field goals in Steelers history with 310.
Boswell went into today's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with 308 career fields goals, needing one to tie and two to pass Anderson. Boswell tied the record with a 52-yard field goal at the end of the first half. He broke the record with a 39-yard field goal in the fourth quarter.
Boswell, who entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Houston Texans following the 2014 NFL Draft, signed a new five-year contract this offseason.
In 2025, Boswell connected on 27 of 32 field goal attempts (84.4%). He was 42 of 43 on extra point attempts (97.7%), accounting for 123 total points.
Boswell connected on a career-long 60-yard field goal in the Steelers Week 1 win over the New York Jets, hitting it with 1:03 remaining in the game for the 34-32 victory. Boswell was named the AFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his game winning effort. Boswell was two for two on field goals, a 56-yarder in the second quarter and the 60-yard field goal.
Boswell also hit two 59-yard field goals in 2025, including Week 10 against the Chargers and Week 16 vs. the Lions.
Boswell had one of his best seasons in 2024 when he was named first team Associated Press All-Pro for the first time in his career. He was also selected to the NFLPA Players' All-Pro team, Sporting News All-Pro, Pro Football Focus All-Pro, the Pro Bowl Games, and Pro Football Writers of America All-NFL and All-AFC teams.
Boswell set a Steelers record for 41 field goals made in 2024, which were the most by a kicker in the NFL since David Akers in 2011 (44) and second-most by a kicker since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger. Boswell also set a Steelers record for most points by a kicker with 158, which was tied for the fifth-most by a kicker since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger.

text:
Reflecting on 25 years at home
Oct 07, 2026 at 08:01 AM
Brian Batko
Contributing Writer/Editor

After a few escalator rides from the Great Hall, you're at the top of the 500 level and the concourse opens up.
That's when my Sunday opened up, and section 509 was the light at the end of the tunnel. For me, as a kid, that was my world eight times a year, give or take.
There were some cold nights, some rainy days and some snowy games in those brightly colored flip-down seats. It went from my parents dropping me off when I was growing up to making the drive myself through the back streets of the North Side leading to the North Shore.
Now Acrisure Stadium hits 25 years since the first game there, back when it was Heinz Field, but always a Steelers fan's sanctuary. I can't remember the specifics of every game I attended, particularly that inaugural game Oct. 7, 2001, a 16-7 win against the Cincinnati Bengals.
But Jerome Bettis rushed for 153 yards that day, and I can still picture his quick feet dancing before following the fullback through a hole. I can still feel the crowd erupt when a smiling-from-ear-to-ear Hines Ward was shown on the scoreboard along with however many receiving yards and touchdowns he racked up that day.
I can still hear the speakers blaring the pregame hype music while players danced in their stretching lines, a melting pot of songs from AC/DC to Young Jeezy. "Back in Black" meant it was back to watching the black and gold.
Waiting for the starters to run out of the tunnel for pregame introductions never got old. It was the "HEEEATH" chant when the offense was announced, and over the years, it's morphed into "MUUUTH" cheers. It was Larry Foote jumping, stomping and grinding the ground underneath him when No. 50 was called onto the field. It was Troy Polamalu flipping the switch to go from mild-mannered man to heat-seeking safety when he put on his helmet.
The 2004 team specifically, sparked by a rookie quarterback named Ben Roethlisberger, sticks out to my 13-year-old self. The back-to-back wins in Pittsburgh against the previously unbeaten Patriots and Eagles on beautiful fall days felt like living in the montage of a sports movie, the part when the home team can't be beat and the newspaper headlines are piling up one after another. It was a football fever dream that left a buzz in the air and a true rush around town.
Same with Roethlisberger's remarkable run at the same point in the calendar a decade later, throwing 12 touchdown passes in two weeks in victories over the Colts and Ravens. It was actually a streak of three wins at home in consecutive weeks, starting with a Monday night versus the Texans.
But Roethlisberger's 522 passing yards in a 51-34 rout of the Colts were tied for the fourth most in NFL history at the time. And he did it in those striped throwback jerseys from 1934. The following Sunday, Roethlisberger found the end zone six times again to help blow out the Ravens, 43-23, setting a two-game NFL record for touchdown passes.

The Steelers have 151 wins all time at Acrisure Stadium, but it's not so much about the numbers. It's about the moments, the magic and the core memories.
There's the AFC championship game in January 2009, pulling away from the Ravens with a Polamalu pick-six to pave the way to a sixth Lombardi Trophy. Or the 2010-11 playoff run, using homefield advantage to hold off the Ravens and Jets en route to another Super Bowl appearance.
More than any one triumph or heartbreak, it's "Renegade" hitting at just the right time. My favorite clip to see on the video board was an excerpt from Joe Greene's Pro Football Hall of Fame induction speech.
"In Pittsburgh, if you're not at the stadium at 1 o'clock on Sunday in the fall, you're in the wrong place," Greene said.
That didn't change when the Steelers moved from Three Rivers Stadium to their new venue. They simply found a home just for football.
The vibe is probably too gritty around here to call it a football palace. It's more of a football fortress. And a quarter-century later, it's still a great place for players to forge a legacy and for Steelers Nation to soak it all in like I did.

Head Coach
Mike McCarthy
Head Coach
The Steelers made it official on Tuesday, January 27, 2026, introducing Mike McCarthy as their 17th head coach in team history. McCarthy becomes only the fourth head coach hired by the Steelers since 1969.
McCarthy brings 18 seasons of experience as a head coach in the NFL, 13 seasons with the Green Bay Packers (2006-18) and five seasons with the Dallas Cowboys (2020-24).
Profile

Offense
Brian Angelichio
Offensive Coordinator
Brian Angelichio is in his first season as the Steelers’ offensive coordinator in 2026. He most recently served as the tight ends coach/passing game coordinator for the Minnesota Vikings for four years.
With three decades of coaching experience across the collegiate and professional ranks, Angelichio will enter his 15th NFL season. In addition to his tenure in Minnesota (2022-25), he previously served as tight ends coach with Carolina (2020-21), Washington (2019), Green Bay (2016-18), Cleveland (2014-15) and Tampa Bay (2012-13).

My Steelers Account
Wait List Benefits
Join the Season Ticket Wait List
Frequently Asked Questions
HOW MANY SEATS MAY I PURCHASE WITH MY WAIT LIST OFFER?

You may purchase up to four (4) seats.
WHAT GAMES ARE INCLUDED IN THE SEASON TICKET PACKAGE PRICE?

All home games at Acrisure Stadium are included in the season ticket package, from preseason through the final regular season home game.
HOW MUCH DOES A SEAT LICENSE COST?

Seat license fee prices start at $1,500
per seat
and will vary depending on location. Seat license fees are a required purchase for all licensed seat locations within Acrisure Stadium.

(Sideline Club) sections 209-212 and sections 233-236
WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A LICENSED AND AN UNLICENSED SEAT?

A seat license allows the account holder to resell or transfer seat license ownership of seats once they no longer wish to purchase season tickets. For unlicensed seats, season tickets can remain in the account holder's name only. Once the account holder of unlicensed seats no longer wishes to or is no longer able to renew the seats, those seats are returned to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Unlicensed seat locations include
sections 519-526, section 219, section 226, and sections 101 rows A-EE and 144 rows A-JJ, and FLD Section 106 - FLD Section 109.
AM I REQUIRED TO PURCHASE A SEAT LICENSE?

If we have licensed seats available through our office, the seat license fees will be applied to those seat locations. The seat license is a required, one-time, nonrefundable fee, so once it is paid, you are only responsible for purchasing the season ticket package each year.
IF I PURCHASE UNLICENSED SEATS, DO I HAVE TO COMPLETE THE SEAT SELECTION PROCESS EACH SEASON?

No, your unlicensed seats will remain in your name for each season as long as you choose to purchase them. Unlicensed seats do not have an associated seat license, so they also do not have a licensed seat owner. Therefore, your unlicensed seats are renewable to you each year.
IF I PURCHASE AN UNLICENSED SEAT LOCATION, CAN I PURCHASE A LICENSE FOR THAT LOCATION IN THE FUTURE?

No, all unlicensed seat locations are and will remain permanently unlicensed.
WILL I EVER HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO MOVE MY SEAT LOCATION IN FUTURE SEASONS?

The Pittsburgh Steelers have a relocation request process for Season Ticket Holders who wish to relocate within Acrisure Stadium. Each Season Ticket Holder becomes eligible to request a relocation after completing one full season with the team. Requests should be submitted to the Steelers by email and can be made for unlicensed or licensed seat locations.
IF I PURCHASE UNLICENSED SEATS, CAN I STILL POST INDIVIDUAL GAME TICKETS FOR SALE OR ELECTRONICALLY TRANSFER TICKETS TO A FRIEND OR FAMILY MEMBER?

Yes, you are still able to post tickets for sale and transfer individual game tickets through your Account Manager, even if your seats are unlicensed.
WOULD I HAVE ACCESS TO MY SEASON TICKET LOCATION FOR ANY POTENTIAL POSTSEASON GAMES?

Yes, as a Season Ticket Holder, you would have first right of refusal to your seat location for potential postseason games. Each new Season Ticket Holder will receive postseason registration information in mid-August. Postseason games are not a required purchase, but we would love to have you join us at Acrisure Stadium for playoffs!
WHAT HAPPENS IF I DECLINE TO PURCHASE SEASON TICKETS?

You will be able to receive two offers while on the Wait List. We cannot guarantee the offers will take place over two consecutive years, but we typically are able to send your second offer within back to back seasons. You would still hold your same position in line, so you do not have to worry about dropping to the bottom of the list. However, if you do decline your second offer, then you will have to re-sign up for the Wait List.
CAN I STILL BE ON THE WAIT LIST IF I AM ALREADY A SEASON TICKET HOLDER?

No, once you are a season ticket holder, you will be removed from the Wait List and are no longer eligible to purchase tickets through a Wait List offer. This includes season ticket holders who sign up through the
STR Marketplace
.
HOW DO I KNOW WHERE I AM ON THE WAIT LIST AND WHEN I WILL RECEIVE MY OFFER?

We send offers to members of the Wait List by sign-up date. Wait List members are not assigned a number in line. You will receive an offer in accordance with the date you officially became a member of the Wait List. Always keep your contact information up to date on your Wait List account to ensure that you will receive your emailed offer.
HOW DO I UPDATE MY ADDRESS ON MY WAIT LIST RECORD?

To update your address, please email us at
STH@Steelers.com
with your current information.
Too excited to wait? You can purchase a stadium seat license from a current Season Ticket Holder on the Seat License Marketplace.
